findings.what: Global hyperbolicity is presented as a hypothesis of Causality.inextensibleNestedOn_top (NestedCausalities.lean:431) that the cut line lacks. That theorem takes no global hyperbolicity. Its hypotheses are CurveNestedOn, CausallyArcConnected, IsCausal, StronglyCausal, closed J⁺/J⁻ of points, hpast and hfut. Global hyperbolicity is a hypothesis of GloballyHyperbolic.inextensibleNestedOn_top (:448) only. Against :431 the cut line lacks hpast (proved here) and closed J⁺ of points (J⁺(0) = [0,∞)∖{1}, not stated in the file), not GH. 'Lacks two hypotheses at once' should also read 'at least two': CausallyArcConnected is argued to fail and Tarentin is not examined.
findings.fix: Reword: 'not globally hyperbolic (a hypothesis of GloballyHyperbolic.inextensibleNestedOn_top) and 1 is a past endpoint (hpast, a hypothesis of both)'. Optionally add ¬ ∀ x, IsClosed ((cutLine 1).Jplus ⊤ {x}) if the theorem is meant to cover Causality.inextensibleNestedOn_top as well. The theorem's statement is true as it stands. Only its description is off.

findings.what: The REPORT says 'The DEC-167 standing is inside the witness itself ..., so the entry needs no gluing caveat'. The docstring says the witness 'stands in either reading'. But the witness states gluing only for the narrower causality (cutLine 1). Under DEC-167 the wider timelikeLine must also be an ETT causality, and its gluing is not a conjunct. The conclusion is true, since the strict library has Causal.timelikeLine_absolutelyMinimal (Causal/Lines.lean:283) and Causal.timelikeLine_absolutelyMinimalOn (:245), but it is not inside the witness.
